title: She wasn’t running toward something.
paragraphs: She wasn’t running toward something.
She was running away—and still lost.
That’s what makes the story of Lot’s wife so terrifying… and so personal.
Because if we’re honest, many of us are doing the same thing.

Genesis 19 paints the scene with urgency. Fire is about to fall. Judgment is at the door. Angels are literally pulling Lot and his family out of a collapsing city. The command is simple, sharp, non-negotiable:
“Escape for your life. Do not look back.” (Genesis 19:17)

Not hesitate.
Not negotiate.
Don’t look back.
But somewhere between mercy and movement… she paused.
And in one glance—one lingering look—everything stopped.
“But Lot’s wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.” (Genesis 19:26)
That’s it.

No long explanation.
No emotional monologue.
Just a moment… that revealed everything.
And Jesus, centuries later, reaches back into that single scene and drops a warning that echoes through time:
“Remember Lot’s wife.” (Luke 17:32)
Three words.
But they carry weight.

Because this is not just about a woman in ancient Sodom.
This is about the human heart under the pressure of letting go.
Let me speak plain, kapatid.

You can leave a place… and still belong to it.
You can walk away from sin… and still be in love with it.
You can follow God… and secretly wish you were still who you used to be.
That’s the tension.
Lot’s wife didn’t look back because she was curious.
She looked back because she was attached.

Sodom was not just where she lived.
It was what shaped her desires.
Her comforts.
Her identity.

And when God began to destroy what she once called “normal,”
her heart whispered,
“Wait… I’m not ready to lose that.”
So she turned.
Not just her head.
Her affection.
And that glance became a grave.
Listen carefully: the danger was not behind her. The danger was within her.
And this is where it cuts deep for us.
Because some of us have already started walking out.

You’ve stepped away from that toxic relationship.
You’ve distanced yourself from that hidden addiction.
You’ve begun saying no to what once controlled you.
But there’s a quiet grief inside.
You miss it.

Not the destruction… but the feeling.
Not the chains… but the familiarity.
Not the sin… but the version of you that felt powerful, desired, in control.

And that’s where the enemy whispers,
“Just look back.”

Just remember how good it felt.
Just revisit it—one more time.
But Jesus says: Remember Lot’s wife.
Why?
Because looking back is not neutral.
It reveals allegiance.
It exposes what still has your heart.
And if we stay there—if we keep turning inward toward what God called us out from—we risk becoming spiritually stuck.
Frozen.
Like salt.
Preserved in a moment we were supposed to pass through.
But hear me now—this is where grace breaks in like sunrise.
Because the Gospel doesn’t just say, “Don’t look back.”
The Gospel gives you someone better to look at.
Jesus Christ.

Not a rule.
Not a warning alone.
A Person.

Hebrews 12:2 says,
“Fixing our eyes on Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith.”
That’s the secret.

You don’t overcome the past by staring at it less.
You overcome it by seeing Christ more.

See Him on the cross—where your sin was not romantic, but crucified.
See Him in resurrection—where your future is not empty, but alive.
See Him calling you forward—not with condemnation, but with nail-scarred hands full of mercy.
Lot’s wife looked back—and perished.
Peter looked back on his failure—and wept bitterly.
But Peter didn’t stay there.
He looked to Jesus… and was restored.
That is the difference between regret and redemption.
So if you’re in that space right now—half out, half longing, half free, half tied—
this is your moment.
Not to pretend you don’t feel it.
But to surrender what you feel to the One who saves.
You don’t need to go back to what God already judged.
You don’t need to resurrect what Jesus died for.
You don’t need to keep mourning what heaven calls bondage.
Lift your eyes.
Fix your gaze.
Run forward.
Because what’s ahead of you in Christ is not restriction—it is freedom with a future.
And here’s the truth that will set your soul on fire:
There is nothing behind you worth losing your destiny over.
So don’t look back.
Not because you’re afraid…
…but because you’ve seen something better.
Jesus.
And He is worth everything.
Start a conversation that leads to freedom.
Because someone out there is one glance away from going back…
and one encounter away from being set free.
